To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the species richness of vascular plant species can be predicted in a northern landscape with a modest accuracy, and that the best predictors are altitude-related variables and variables that are related to the abundance and the quality of water.

(a) species richness of vascular plant species is highest at the mesoscales where the topographical and geological heterogeneity is highest, and (b) the most important predictors of vascular plant species richness are altitude, length of rivers and streams, steep-sided gorges, and the abundance of gabbros in bedrock.

the species richness of vascular plant taxa in the Kevo subarctic landscape is best predicted by the following factors: (i) length of rivers and streams (ii) relative abundance of gneiss in the bedrock (iii) relative abundance of cliffs and steep-sided valleys (iv) relative abundance of the bedrock type gabbro (v) mean annual temperature (vi) relative abundance of peatland in the grid square (vii) mean annual temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the species richness-environment relationships in the poorly explored northern boreal zone.

the development of predictive models of species richness of plants at the mesoscales, and with the testing of the available energy hypothesis as an explanatory model of species richness-environment relationships.
the species richness of vascular plant species and its relationship to the environment in northern Finland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the models are useful for predicting the patterns of vascular plant species richness in the poorly explored meso-scale, but that they cannot be used to predict species richness in the absence of a detailed field work.
the patterns of vascular plant richness in the subarctic are not easily predictable with the available environmental information.
, in the Kevo subarctic region, vascular plant species richness is positively related to energy-related factors, such as altitude and solar radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of the species richness predictions is not high, and that the models should be used only as a first screening tool for identifying areas of potential high species richness.
the accuracy of the models is not sufficient to predict species richness of vascular plant taxa with a precision of 1-2 species in the landscape of Kevo.

the derived models can be used for a rough estimation of species richness of plants at the mesoscales, and that they provide a good starting point for the planning of future field work in subarctic landscapes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of predictions of vascular plant richness is modest in the subarctic region, and that field work should be conducted to verify predictions of species richness at the landscape scale.

the patterns of species distribution in the poorly explored subarctic landscape can be successfully predicted by using simple and easily available variables, which are also easily accessible in remote areas, such as the Kevo subarctic landscape.
the models can be used to prioritize field work in a subarctictaiga landscape.
